title: Dravidian languages - Wikipedia
text: Dravidian languages are mostly located in the southern and central parts of south Asia with 2 main outliers, Brahui having speakers in Balochistan and as far north as Merv, Turkmenistan, and Kurukh to the east in Jharkhand and as far northeast as Bhutan, Nepal and Assam.

title: Gondi, Northern | Ethnologue Free
text: Northern Gondi is a stable indigenous language of India. It belongs to the Dravidian language family and is part of the Gondi macrolanguage. The language is used as a first language by all in the ethnic community.

title: Gondi language
text: Gondi (Gōṇḍī; natively Kōī or Kōītōr), is a South-Central Dravidian language spoken by the Gondi people, an indigenous group primarily inhabiting central and east-central India.
